steps: Sign in to the parent SendGrid account as the account owner or an admin teammate (an API key can't have more permissions than you).
Go to Settings > API Keys and click Create API Key.
Type a name in the API Key Name box and choose Custom Access.
Give read access to API Keys, Security, SSO Settings and Teammates, and no access to everything else.
Click Create & View, then click the key to copy it; it's displayed only once.
permissions: access_settings.whitelist.read - GET /access_settings/whitelist (listed under Security in the UI)
sendgrid.plan_note: SSO is available only on Email API Pro, Premier and Marketing Campaigns Advanced plans, so the SSO checks can't pass on other plans. Free and Essentials plans allow one teammate.
sendgrid.token_lifetime: Does not expire; valid until you delete the key.

compatibility.detail: EU host selectable.

caveats: If IP Access Management is on, add the collector's egress IP to the allow list; SendGrid blocks UI, API and SMTP access from other IPs.
SendGrid lists the API keys that belong to the authenticated user, so create this key from the parent account rather than a subuser.

fields.label: Management console URL
fields.help: Host name of your SentinelOne management console, without https://.

fields.label: API token
fields.help: The service user's API token.

steps: Sign in to the SentinelOne Management Console as an Admin at Account (or Global) scope.
Go to Settings > Users > Service Users and select Actions > Create New Service User.
Enter a Name, choose an Expiration Date, and click Next.
Set the scope of access to your Account, select the Viewer role, and click Create User.
Copy the API token now; it is displayed only once.
Enter your console host name and the API token here.
sentinelone.permissions: Built-in Viewer role (read-only) at Account scope. A Site-scoped token only returns that site's agents and console users.
sentinelone.token_lifetime: Expires on the Expiration Date set when the service user is created; the date cannot be changed afterwards.

compatibility.detail: ApiToken prefix added by the connector; cursor paging.

caveats: Not verified against SentinelOne's own documentation, which requires a console login; the steps follow current partner guides (Palo Alto Networks, SonicWall, Secureworks) and menu names can vary by console version.
Use Account scope so every site's endpoints and console users are included.
The firewall check reads whether SentinelOne Firewall Control is enabled for the agent's group, not the operating-system firewall.
Create a new service user and update the connection before the token's expiration date.

fields.label: Auth token
fields.help: Copied from the Tokens section of your internal integration.

fields.label: Sentry host
fields.help: sentry.io, or us.sentry.io / de.sentry.io to keep API calls in your data region; self-hosted: your Sentry host.

steps: Sign in to Sentry with an organization role of Manager or Admin.
Click Settings in the left menu, then Custom Integrations, and press Create New Integration.
Select Internal Integration, press Next, and enter a name.
Under Permissions, set Organization, Project and Member to Read; leave the rest at No Access.
Click Save Changes, scroll down to Tokens, and copy the generated token.
sentry.permissions: Organization: Read (org:read), Project: Read (project:read), Member: Read (member:read).
sentry.token_lifetime: Does not expire; revoke it manually (up to 20 tokens per internal integration).

compatibility.detail: Projects per organization; Link-header paging; host selectable; isPublic check dropped.

caveats: Internal integration tokens cover the whole organization and don't depend on a user; personal tokens only list projects on your own teams.
You can't give an integration more permissions than your own role has.
Your data region is shown on your organization's settings page.
Self-hosted Sentry must be reachable from the collector over HTTPS.

servicenow.credential: ServiceNow integration user (User ID and password) for Table API basic authentication

fields.label: Instance URL
fields.help: Your instance host without https://.

fields.label: User ID
fields.help: The integration user's User ID (its login name, not an email address).

fields.label: Password
fields.help: Set with Set Password on the user record.

steps: Sign in to your instance as an administrator (creating users requires the user_admin role).
Navigate to All > User Administration > Users and select New.
Enter a User ID and name, select Web service access only (or set Identity type to Machine), and select Submit.
Open the new user, select Set Password, and set a strong password.
Assign roles: itil, plus read access to sys_audit and sys_user_has_role (for example admin together with snc_read_only).
Enter your instance host, the User ID and the password here.
servicenow.permissions: Read access to sys_user, change_request, incident, sys_audit and sys_user_has_role. itil covers incidents and change requests and contains snc_platform_rest_api_access (Table API access). sys_audit and sys_user_has_role are typically restricted to admin: pair admin with snc_read_only (blocks inserts, updates and deletes on all tables) or grant table read ACLs to a custom role.
servicenow.token_lifetime: Password credential with no token expiry; it stays valid until changed or expired by your instance's password policy.

compatibility.detail: Basic auth (User ID in the email field, password in the token field) against https://{domain}/api/now/table/{tableName} matches the Table API, and all five GETs use documented sysparm_query, sysparm_fields and sysparm_limit parameters. sysparm_limit is applied before ACL evaluation, so missing read access can return empty results instead of an error.

caveats: Not fully verified: ServiceNow's docs don't list which roles can read sys_audit and sys_user_has_role; confirm the read ACLs on your instance.
If the user can't read a table, ServiceNow can return an empty list instead of an error, so the audit-logging check may fail falsely and the admin-count check may show not assessed.
If you grant admin to this user, it is counted in the active-admin check.
snc_read_only requires the Read-Only User Role (com.snc.read_only.role) plugin.
If your instance restricts the Table API with REST API access policies, allow Basic Auth for this user.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: From the service account's Keys tab; the value is shown only once.

fields.label: SigNoz URL
fields.help: Instance host without https:// (Cloud: <tenant>.<region>.signoz.cloud; self-hosted: e.g. signoz.example.com).

steps: Sign in to SigNoz with the signoz-admin role.
Go to Settings > Service Accounts, click New Service Account, enter a name (lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens) and click Create.
Open the service account and, in the Overview tab, assign the signoz-viewer role, then click Save.
Switch to the Keys tab, click Add Key, enter a key name, optionally set an expiration date, and click Create.
Copy the key value immediately.
signoz.permissions: Managed role signoz-viewer (read-only); it covers GET /api/v1/service_accounts/me (the connection test), GET /api/v2/dashboards and GET /api/v2/rules.
signoz.plan_note: Self-hosted SigNoz must be v0.129.0 or later (dashboards v2 API); Service Accounts were introduced in v0.118.0.
signoz.token_lifetime: No expiry unless you set an expiration date; the date can be changed or removed later.

compatibility.detail: The SIGNOZ-API-KEY header and https://{domain} match SigNoz's docs, and GET /api/v2/dashboards and /api/v2/rules allow signoz-viewer. /api/v2/dashboards only exists from v0.129.0 (June 2026) and /api/v2/rules from v0.120.0, so older self-hosted instances return 404 for those checks. GET /api/v1/version is unauthenticated, so the connection test passes even with an invalid key; switch it to GET /api/v1/service_accounts/me, which SigNoz documents for validating keys.

caveats: Only admins can create service accounts and keys by default.
Self-hosted instances must be reachable from the collector over HTTPS.

slack.credential: User OAuth Token (xoxp-) from a Slack app installed by a Workspace Admin or Owner

fields.label: User OAuth Token
fields.help: Starts with xoxp-; listed under OAuth Tokens on your app's OAuth & Permissions page.

steps: Make sure you're a Workspace Admin or Owner; Slack only shows members' 2FA status to admins.
Go to api.slack.com/apps, create an app, select Blank app and click Continue, enter an App Name, select your Workspace and click Create.
Open OAuth & Permissions; under Scopes > User Token Scopes, click Add an OAuth Scope and add users:read and users:read.email.
Click Install to Workspace and select Allow.
Copy the User OAuth Token (xoxp-) from OAuth Tokens.
slack.permissions: User Token Scopes: users:read and users:read.email (auth.test needs no scope). The installing user must be a Workspace Admin or Owner.
slack.token_lifetime: Does not expire unless token rotation is enabled for the app (rotated tokens expire every 12 hours).

compatibility.detail: Admin user token required for has_2fa; members paged; deleted users and bots skipped.

caveats: Use the User OAuth Token (xoxp-), not the Bot User OAuth Token; bot tokens can't see 2FA status.
Don't enable token rotation for this app, or the token expires every 12 hours.
On Enterprise Grid, install the app to the workspace rather than org-wide.

snyk.credential: Group service account token (Group Viewer role)

fields.label: Service account token
fields.help: The token Snyk showed when you created the service account.

fields.label: API host
fields.help: Leave blank for SNYK-US-01 (app.snyk.io); SNYK-US-02: api.us.snyk.io, SNYK-EU-01: api.eu.snyk.io, SNYK-AU-01: api.au.snyk.io.

steps: Sign in to Snyk as a Group Admin.
Select your Group and go to Settings > Service accounts (new navigation: Settings > Security and access > Service accounts).
Create a service account with a unique name and the Group Viewer role; do not select OAuth 2.0 client credentials.
Copy the token as soon as it is displayed; Snyk shows it only once.
snyk.permissions: Group Viewer role on a Group-level service account, the read-only option Snyk documents. It grants View Organization (org.read), View Projects (org.project.read) and View Project history (org.project.snapshot.read) in every Organization of the Group, covering GET /rest/orgs, /orgs/{org_id}/projects, /orgs/{org_id}/issues and /orgs/{org_id}/settings/sast.
snyk.plan_note: Snyk API access and service accounts require a Snyk Enterprise plan.
snyk.token_lifetime: Access-token service accounts expire on their expiry date (at most 1 year after creation); legacy API-key service accounts do not expire.

compatibility.detail: token prefix added; region host selectable; links.next followed.

caveats: Do not use OAuth 2.0 client credentials: those access tokens are short-lived (1 hour by default) and are not supported here.
Personal access tokens also authenticate, but they expire within 90 days and carry the user's full permissions.

fields.label: Personal access token
fields.help: Generated in SonarQube Cloud under My account > Access Tokens; it acts with your user's permissions.

fields.label: Instance
fields.help: Leave blank for sonarcloud.io; US-region organizations: sonarqube.us.

steps: Sign in to SonarQube Cloud (sonarcloud.io) as a user who is a member of each organization to monitor and can browse all of its projects.
Open your account menu in the top right corner and select My account > Access Tokens.
Under Generate Tokens, enter a token name and select an expiration period (7, 30, 60 or 90 days, or Custom up to 1 year).
Select Generate Token and copy the value immediately; it cannot be retrieved later.
sonarcloud.permissions: Personal access tokens have no scopes and act with all of the user's permissions, so read-only restriction is not possible. The user must be a member of each organization (api/qualitygates/list and api/organizations/search?member=true require it) and have Browse permission on its projects (api/projects/search returns only projects the user can access).
sonarcloud.token_lifetime: Expires after the period you choose (7 to 90 days, or a custom date up to 1 year); a token without an expiration date is removed after 60 days of inactivity.

compatibility.detail: Region host selectable; connection test rejects bad tokens.

caveats: A personal token carries all of its user's permissions; prefer a user without organization admin rights.
Projects the token's user cannot browse are left out of the checks.

fields.label: Restricted API key
fields.help: Created on the API keys page in live mode; Stripe shows the value only once.

steps: Sign in to the Stripe Dashboard in live mode with the Administrator or Developer role.
Open the API keys page and click Create restricted key, starting from zero permissions.
Enter a Key name, then set Read for Webhook Endpoints and Events.
Leave every other resource set to None.
Click Create key, complete the two-factor verification, and copy the key value.
stripe.permissions: Read on Webhook Endpoints (GET /v1/webhook_endpoints, also the connection test) and Events (GET /v1/events). All other resources: None.
stripe.token_lifetime: Does not expire unless you expire or rotate it in the Dashboard.

compatibility.detail: Connection test uses /webhook_endpoints.

caveats: Use a live-mode key; sandbox keys (rk_test_) only see test data.
If the key has an access policy (IP or ASN allowlist), allow the collector's outbound addresses.
Stripe lists events from the last 30 days only, so the event-log check fails on accounts with no recent activity.

supabase.credential: Personal access token (scoped, if available on your account)

fields.label: Access token
fields.help: Generated on your account's Access Tokens page; starts with sbp_.

steps: Sign in to the Supabase Dashboard with an account that has a role in each organization to monitor (Read-Only is enough).
Open your Access Tokens page (supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens) and generate a new token.
If permission options appear, scope the token to the projects to monitor and grant Read for Projects (account-wide), SSL Enforcement, Network Restrictions and Backups.
Set the token's expiry, create it and copy the token.
supabase.permissions: Scoped token: Projects (account-wide) - Read; SSL Enforcement - Read; Network Restrictions - Read; Backups - Read. A classic token has your account's full access, and no token can exceed your organization role.
supabase.plan_note: Daily backups exist only for Pro, Team and Enterprise plan projects. The Read-Only organization role is only available on Team and Enterprise plans.
supabase.token_lifetime: Expires on the custom expiry you set when generating it.

compatibility.detail: Bearer auth and https://api.supabase.com/v1 are correct. GET /projects, /projects/{ref}/ssl-enforcement, /projects/{ref}/network-restrictions and /projects/{ref}/database/backups exist and return the fields we read (ref, currentConfig.database, config.dbAllowedCidrs, walg_enabled). The SSL-enforcement and network-restrictions endpoints are flagged experimental (Beta) and may change.

caveats: Scoped tokens are in public alpha. If you can't choose permissions, you get a classic token with full access to all your organizations and projects.
Free plan projects have no daily backups and will fail the backup check.
Create a new token and update it here before the old one expires.

fields.label: API access token
fields.help: Generated on the Keys page of the Tailscale admin console; it starts with tskey-api-.

steps: Sign in as an Owner, Admin, IT admin or Network admin of the tailnet (a Network admin can read but not change devices).
Open the Keys page of the admin console.
In the API access tokens section, select Generate access token.
Choose the number of days until it expires (1 to 90), generate the token, and copy it.
Paste the token here and note its expiry date so you can replace it in time.
tailscale.permissions: API access tokens can't be scoped; they have the same permissions as the user who created them. The collector only lists tailnet devices, which every admin role can read. The read-only scope devices:core:read exists only for trust credentials (OAuth clients), which this connector can't use yet.
tailscale.plan_note: The Tailscale API is available on all plans; the Network admin and IT admin roles require the Standard, Premium or Enterprise plan.
tailscale.token_lifetime: Expires after 1 to 90 days (you choose); it can't be set to never expire.

compatibility.detail: Authorization: Bearer tskey-api-... is accepted, and GET https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2/tailnet/-/devices ('-' is the token's default tailnet) returns authorized, keyExpiryDisabled, updateAvailable and isExternal in its default field set. Read-only trust credentials (OAuth client with devices:core:read) would need a client-credentials exchange at https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2/oauth/token (tokens last 1 hour), which we don't perform.

caveats: API access tokens can't be made read-only; where your plan allows, generate the token from a Network admin account so it can't approve or remove devices.
The token stops working after the number of days you chose (90 at most); generate a new one and update it here before then.
API access tokens belong to the individual user who created them.

tenable.credential: API keys (Access Key and Secret Key)

fields.label: Access key
fields.help: From the API user's API Keys section.

fields.label: Secret key
fields.help: Shown once, together with the access key.

fields.label: Tenable host
fields.help: Leave blank for cloud.tenable.com; FedRAMP: fedcloud.tenable.com.

steps: Sign in to Tenable Vulnerability Management as an Administrator.
In the left navigation, click Settings, then the Access Control tile, then the Users tab.
Click Create User, choose the Scan Manager role (Administrator if you need the failed-login check), select API Key under Authentication, and click Save.
Open the new user and, in the API Keys section, click Generate API Keys, then Replace & Generate.
Copy the Access Key and Secret Key before leaving the page; they cannot be shown again.
Enter the Access Key and Secret Key here.
tenable.permissions: Scan Manager [40] role for GET /scanners (or the custom role privilege VM.VM_SENSOR.VM_SCANNER.READ), plus the Can View [16] scan permission on the scans to report (or the custom role privilege VM.VM_SCAN.VM_SCAN.READ) for GET /scans. GET /users needs Basic [16] but returns login_fail_count only to Administrator [64] users, so the failed-login check needs an Administrator, which is not read-only.
tenable.token_lifetime: No expiry is documented; keys stay valid until they are regenerated (which replaces them) or the user is disabled.

compatibility.detail: X-ApiKeys built from access and secret keys; /server/properties; FedRAMP host selectable.

caveats: Generating keys replaces the user's existing keys immediately; update the connection afterwards.
If Generate API Keys is unavailable, API Key authentication is not enabled for that user.
Scans are only listed if the API user can view them; grant Can View on every scan you want covered.
The keys work across all Tenable One products your organization licenses, so store them securely.

twilio.credential: Main API key (API key SID and secret)

fields.label: API key SID
fields.help: Starts with SK; shown with the key after you create it.

fields.label: API key secret
fields.help: Shown only once, when the key is created.

steps: Sign in to the Twilio Console for your main (parent) account and use the Legacy Console; the new Console only creates Standard and Restricted keys.
Click Admin > Account management in the top right corner.
Under Keys & credentials, click API keys & tokens, then click Create API key.
Enter a Friendly name, select the United States (US1) Region and the key type Main.
Click Create, copy the SID and the secret, select the Got it! checkbox and click Done.
twilio.permissions: Key type Main. Twilio requires a Main key (or Account SID and Auth Token) for the Accounts and Keys endpoints; Standard keys can't call them, so read-only access isn't possible for these calls.
twilio.token_lifetime: No expiry is documented; the key works until you delete it.

compatibility.detail: Pages by next_page_uri.

caveats: A Main key has full account access, equivalent to your Auth Token; store it securely and delete it when it's no longer needed.
Create the key in your main (parent) account so its subaccounts are included.
API credentials are region-specific; use a United States (US1) key.

vercel.credential: Access token scoped to a team (All Projects)

fields.label: Access token
fields.help: Created on the Account Tokens page; starts with vcp_ and is shown only once.

steps: Make sure you're a member of the Vercel team to monitor.
In the dashboard's scope selector (top left), switch to your personal account, then open the Account Tokens page under Settings.
Enter a descriptive token name.
Open Scope, select the team, then select All Projects.
Choose an expiration and select Create.
Copy the token now; Vercel shows it only once.
vercel.permissions: Scope: your team with All Projects. Vercel tokens can't be read-only: they can read and write that team's resources on your behalf.
vercel.plan_note: SAML SSO requires Enterprise, or Pro with the SAML SSO add-on.
vercel.token_lifetime: Expires on the expiration you choose at creation.

compatibility.detail: Team-scoped token per team; projects and members paged.

caveats: Use Team scope with All Projects: a Full Account token misses team projects, and a single-project token can't read team data.
Add a separate connection for each Vercel team.
Teams that enforce two-factor authentication or SAML may require it before you can create a token for them.
Create a new token and update it here before the expiration date.

fields.label: Zendesk subdomain
fields.help: Your {subdomain}.zendesk.com address, without https://.

fields.label: OAuth client identifier
fields.help: The Identifier field of the OAuth client in Admin Center.

fields.label: OAuth client secret
fields.help: Shown in full only once, after you save the OAuth client.

steps: Make sure you're a Zendesk admin with permission to manage OAuth clients.
In Admin Center, go to Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients and click Add OAuth client.
Enter a Name, note the Identifier, and set Client kind to Confidential.
Under Scopes, select users:read.
Save the client and copy the Secret right away; it's displayed in full only once.
zendesk.permissions: users:read (View users) on the OAuth client and token request. List Users is allowed for admins, agents and light agents; the token acts as the user associated with the client.
zendesk.plan_note: OAuth clients are available on all Suite plans (Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, Enterprise Plus) and on Support Team, Professional and Enterprise.
zendesk.token_lifetime: Access tokens from the client credentials grant expire (30 minutes by default for clients created on or after April 30, 2026; 5 minutes to 2 days if set) and have no refresh token.

compatibility.detail: Client-credentials token exchange; Zendesk policy on customer OAuth clients applies.

caveats: Don't use a Zendesk API token: no new tokens after October 27, 2026, and all stop working on April 30, 2027.
Zendesk's developer policy says third-party apps must not use your API tokens or your own OAuth client; check with your Zendesk admin before connecting.
Enter your {subdomain}.zendesk.com address, as used in Zendesk's API docs.

zoom.credential: Server-to-Server OAuth app (Account ID, Client ID, Client secret)

fields.label: Account ID
fields.help: Shown on the app's App credentials page.

fields.label: Client ID
fields.help: Shown on the app's App credentials page.

fields.label: Client secret
fields.help: Shown on the app's App credentials page; keep it secret.

steps: Ask a Zoom admin to enable View and Edit for Server-to-Server OAuth app on your role (User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features) and to grant the admin permissions behind the scopes below.
In the Zoom App Marketplace, click Developer in the lower-left navigation, then on Created apps click Develop and select Build an app.
Select Server-to-Server OAuth app and click Create.
On App credentials, copy the Account ID, Client ID and Client secret.
Fill in Information (developer name and email are required), then under Scopes click Add Scopes and add the scopes listed below.
Activate the app.
zoom.permissions: Granular scopes: user:read:list_users:admin (List users), user:read:user:admin (Get a user), role:read:list_roles:admin (List roles).
zoom.plan_note: List roles requires a Pro or higher plan.
zoom.token_lifetime: Access tokens expire after 1 hour with no refresh token; a new one is requested with the app credentials. Deactivating the app invalidates existing tokens.

compatibility.detail: Server-to-Server OAuth token exchange; pending users listed separately; Master-only managed domains dropped.

caveats: Keep the app activated; deactivating it stops the connection.
If the app owner loses admin-level role permissions, Zoom removes the admin scopes from the app.
